sonnet.problem: Story card 3 already tells that the LORD will sling the people out of the land. True/false card 4 just repeats that claim, so it gives the answer away and tests nothing new.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: Card 9 already tested that the sons are gone and no longer help. Card 10 re-asks the same fact, and its question says 'With the sons gone and the tent torn down', which hands over the answer 'No one at all'.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: The story card says verse 23 is about 'who's really in charge of a person's path'. That signals the answer to true/false card 6, that no one who walks directs his own steps.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
